solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Come out again to harvest fruit

parts.note: to harvest a crop is to reap it
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An instruction to go out once more and gather the orchard's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to show up a second time after vanishing, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Calm attitude backing head of state up

indicators.note: backing means the attitude comes behind the reversed royal letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, head of state
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A cool stance supporting the national leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means read upwards, and 'backing' means coming behind, so the attitude follows. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of calm rest and tranquillity.

clue.text: Is cracking transmutation of metal her concern primarily?

definitions.text: Is cracking transmutation of metal her concern primarily?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the word is goes inside the rest
transmutation means change of form, so these letters are rearranged
primarily picks the opening letters of her and concern

parts.note: taken as the word is itself

explanation.surface: Is turning base metals into gold what she mostly cares about?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: 'transmutation of' metal was exactly the alchemist's quest, while signalling the anagram; 'cracking' and 'primarily' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist sought to transmute base metals into gold, so that was the chief concern.

clue.text: Trial of man responsible for death of Jesus reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the answer is how the name is said when spoken

parts.words: man responsible for death of Jesus
parts.note: Pontius Pilate ordered the crucifixion

explanation.surface: The trial of Pontius Pilate for crucifying Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface trial suggests a court case, but the definition means a test run.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial or test version, as in a pilot scheme or TV pilot.

clue.text: Desire for money is at the heart of German state church

indicators.note: the heart is the inside, so the state loses its outer letters

parts.note: Bavaria is a German federal state
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Greed lies at the core of a German state's church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the heart of' trims BAVARIA to AVARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, especially a hunger for wealth.

clue.text: Unofficial call to block further education

indicators.note: one piece is put in the way of, so sits inside, the letters of the other

parts.note: FE is the abbreviation for further education, British post-school colleges
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: An unauthorised phone call holds up a college's further education plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to block' signals insertion. Further education means British colleges for students past school age.
explanation.definitionFit: Fringe events, like the Edinburgh Fringe, are the unofficial ones held alongside a main festival.

clue.text: Easing up on branch hoarding new money

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: hoarding means storing away inside, so the branch holds the other letters

parts.note: a leg is a branch, as of a journey
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Becoming lenient over a bank branch stockpiling freshly minted cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting is softening or becoming less severe, which is easing up.

clue.text: Openings in new international markets begin interesting shower producers

indicators.note: openings are starts, so take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: New global markets open with intriguing launches.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain-bearing clouds, which produce showers.

clue.text: English final filled with uncertainty is improving

indicators.note: filled with means the doubt word goes inside

parts.note: dying as in dying words, the final ones
an if is an uncertainty, as in ifs and buts

explanation.surface: An English cup final full of doubt is improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Edifying means morally or intellectually uplifting, improving the mind.

clue.text: Funny games cut short by author of fiction

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word cut itself
a liar is someone who makes up fictions

explanation.surface: Some games get curtailed by a novelist, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CUT to CU. 'author of fiction' is a playful way of saying someone who invents untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of odd or strange, as in a funny feeling, is peculiar.

clue.text: Former pupils upset Milan University dons

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the shuffled city name wears the next letter inside it
upset means the letters of Milan are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Academic staff at a university in Milan are upset by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MILAN into ALMNI; 'dons' has it put on U, which goes inside. Dons looks like university teachers but means puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are the graduates or old students of a school or college.

clue.text: Eat out in France and Switzerland

parts.note: et is French for and
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Dining out in France and Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' looks like dining in restaurants, but it means corrode away.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design by letting acid corrode the surface.

clue.text: Women in parliamentary constituency do difficult work

indicators.note: the letter for women sits inside the word for the constituency

parts.note: a seat is a constituency an MP represents

explanation.surface: Female candidates in a constituency must put in hard graft.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over something is to labour hard at it, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Strengthen fine wines, ultimately breaking tiny rum bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so one group of letters encloses the other
rum means odd or strange, so the letters of tiny are rearranged
breaking means the letters of fine plus the last of wines are broken up and reordered
ultimately points to the final letter of the word wines

explanation.surface: Fortified wines break small bottles of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams, one inside another: 'rum' (odd, not the drink) works on tiny, 'breaking' on fine plus the end of wines, and 'bottles' holds the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify something is to make it stronger or more acute.

clue.text: Easy test in which top mark goes to first person

indicators.note: one letter is given away and becomes another, so the swap is signalled

parts.note: a sample is a small test portion
A is the top grade in exams
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An easy exam where the best grade is awarded to whoever finishes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and easy both describe a task needing little effort.

clue.text: Seemingly, primitive defiles standards of etiquette

parts.note: proto- means first or primitive
cols are mountain passes, also called defiles

explanation.surface: A primitive person apparently tramples on good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' admits the answer only looks like primitive passes. Defiles reads as pollutes but is a noun for passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocols are the formal rules of correct conduct, diplomatic etiquette.

clue.text: Restriction in Barnet Hospital being shown briefly about parking

indicators.note: about means one piece is wrapped around the parking letter
briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a programme that is airing is being shown

explanation.surface: Parking restrictions at Barnet Hospital, a London hospital, get a brief airing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims AIRING to AIRIN; 'about' puts it round P. Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), and also a London borough, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a clip that holds hair in place, so it restrains one's locks.

clue.text: Sharp drop in cost covering essential ingredients of recipe

indicators.note: covering means the cost word goes around the other letters

parts.note: price means cost

indicators.note: the essential part is the core, so take the inner letters of recipe

explanation.surface: A sudden fall in what the core ingredients of a dish cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A precipice is a cliff face, a steep drop.

clue.text: A French girl from Paris died hungry?

parts.note: un is French for a
fille is French for girl

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman perished from starvation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that hungry is defined loosely, as not filled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hungry has a stomach not filled, so unfilled is a playful fit.

clue.text: Try to make contacts in the fishing industry?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... is the job of fishermen with nets

explanation.surface: Building contacts as a fisherman would.
explanation.definitionFit: Networking means mixing to form business connections; separately, net work is fishing with nets.

clue.text: What may be found in snorkel, perhaps?

definitions.text: What may be found in snorkel, perhaps?

indicators.note: found in means the answer is concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something a diver might come across while snorkelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a definition: seaweed is what a snorkeller might find.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp is a large seaweed, the sort of thing seen underwater with a snorkel.

clue.text: Current doctor probing bird and animal shelter

indicators.note: probing means pushing inside, so the letters go into the bird

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
I is the symbol for electric current
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor examines a bird and an animal shelter on the current visit.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN as female swan is a common crossword bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigpen is a sty, an enclosure housing pigs.

clue.text: What may be used for last bit of defragging memory?

definitions.text: What may be used for last bit of defragging memory?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the last bit is the final letter of the word defragging

parts.note: RAM is random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A computer user wonders what tool finishes tidying the memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a defragging utility is a program.
explanation.definitionFit: Defragmentation is done by software, a program run on the computer's storage.

clue.text: What might cause one to start quarrel about king?

definitions.text: What might cause one to start

indicators.note: about means the quarrel word goes round the king letter

parts.note: a fight is a quarrel
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A query about what makes someone begin an argument over a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' looks like begin, but means jump with alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock that makes one jump.

clue.text: Messy situation involving criminal mob and oil rig

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or twisted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tangled affair in which gangsters are mixed up with an offshore platform.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, embarrassing tangle or muddle.

clue.text: Put fat on bottom when eating tons

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the bottom word holds the tons letter

parts.note: the base is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: Putting on weight around the backside from eating a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat or juices over meat as it roasts.

clue.text: He's backed service embracing religious teaching

definitions.note: the clue speaks of what a friar is: he is one

indicators.note: embracing means the reversed letters hold the next piece inside
backed means the service's letters are reversed

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force, an armed service
RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A man supports a church service that includes Bible study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns RAF into FAR; 'embracing' puts RI in it. The definition is cheeky: He's stands for a friar is.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a male member of a mendicant religious order, so he is a man of the church.

clue.text: Recurring feature of idiotic fool spoiled part of book

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters are messed up and rearranged

parts.note: the letter i recurs three times in the word idiotic

explanation.surface: A daft fool ruined a section of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' shuffles I with FOOL. The I is a letter that keeps turning up in idiotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a leaf of a book, or a page number.

clue.text: Part of what forms individual is somewhat flexible

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A component of a person's make-up is fairly pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means lithe and supple, moving with ease.

clue.text: Exercising again and again is boring

definitions.meaning: rehearsing by repetition, as soldiers do

explanation.definitionFit: Drill means repetitive training and also to bore a hole, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Formal and dull cases persist regularly

indicators.note: cases means the dull word encloses the following letters

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting

indicators.note: regularly points to every other letter of the word persist

explanation.surface: Formal, tedious legal cases go on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and suited to a formal occasion.

clue.text: Rotten, corrupt, Independent politician ousting Republican unable to function in Congress

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: corrupt means the remaining letters are rearranged
ousting means the Republican letter is thrown out of the word rotten

explanation.surface: A corrupt independent lawmaker pushes out a Republican and gets nothing done in Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' takes R from ROTTEN to leave OTTEN; 'corrupt' rearranges it to OTENT. Congress here is sexual intercourse, not the American legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means powerless, especially unable to perform sexually, which is the innuendo here.
